children: This is an edition of the WSJ Weekend Reads newsletter, a weekly look at our most colorful, thought-provoking and original feature stories on the business of life. If you're not subscribed, sign up here.

He was valedictorian at Columbia University at age 19. He thought about becoming a Supreme Court justice but instead went to Silicon Valley, where he developed a reputation as "the Nostradamus of AI." Then last month, just two days before his wedding, Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund unraveled.
This week, Berber Jin, Ben Cohen and Anissa Gardizy give us a deep dive into Aschenbrenner's past, hard lessons for Wall Street and implications for the ethical future of AI.
In other news, homeowners say mold is making it difficult to breathe and costs millions in repairs and healthcare bills. Builders say the rise in mold-related lawsuits is targeting them unfairly.
And we highlight a 500-mile walk through Spain for a woman contemplating her next move in life.

Enjoy your weekend with these and all the great reads below. It's a bit of a break for Cristina Lourosa-Ricardo, who regularly writes this newsletter. I'm happy to take over the keyboard this week and next.

Leopold Aschenbrenner was hailed as a visionary in artificial intelligence. His hedge fund was managing $45 billion in assets. But now Wall Street sees him as the latest cautionary tale of hubris-an inexperienced investor taking on too much risk.
Mold is driving America's homeowners crazy, and they want builders to pay. Builders say the allegations aren't merited and the lawsuits are costing millions.
Owners of a home in New York transformed it into a $2.9 million luxury retreat for their bearded collie named Buster.
Sumathi Reddy says you don't need to upend your day by constantly trying to drink more water. Happily, coffee and sparkling water count toward the fluid your body needs.
A young woman who lost her job searches for her own new path along Spain's Camino de Santiago.
When AI Is Your New Sibling
Columnist Jamie Waters was surprised when his parents became obsessed with Claude, the chatbot. Or, as his mom calls it, "The nice man who answers all my questions."
Today's bride doesn't need millions of followers on social media to find brands willing to help sponsor wedding costs.
A recent survey found that 91% of security professionals in the U.S. and Europe have no formal road map in place to protect against the threat of quantum computing.
Managers are expecting a work blackout in November when employees who've waited 13 years for a new "Grand Theft Auto" installment take an unofficial holiday.
Olivia Dean speaks about obliterating a record held by Abba, toppling Jay-Z and Rihanna's "Umbrella" and why meeting Stevie Wonder almost did her in.
